synthesizedFacts.fact: Idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis is a benign condition characterized by small white spots on sun-exposed areas of the skin.
Tinea versicolor is a common fungal infection that can cause white patches on the skin, often exacerbated by warm and humid conditions.
Vitiligo is an autoimmune condition leading to the loss of skin pigmentation, resulting in white patches.
Topical treatments like corticosteroids and retinoids can help reduce the appearance of white sun spots.
Laser therapy and microdermabrasion are potential treatments for persistent white spots caused by sun damage.
